description: Establish a verifiable baseline for the i18n system before making changes. Confirm the environment can run the primary verification gate (the i18n audit script) and capture its current output so later features can be compared against a known-good starting point. No source changes in this feature.
steps: Confirm tooling: run `node --version` (host is v22; .nvmrc pins 24 but the audit script is plain Node ESM and runs on 22) and `pnpm --version`.

Run the primary i18n gate `node scripts/i18n-audit.mjs --ci` from repo root and capture the full output. Record the current key counts (en=2019 keys; non-en locales ~58% complete) and confirm exit code 0.

Run `node scripts/i18n-audit.mjs --duplicates --dangling --placeholders --plurals` and record the output so regressions introduced later are attributable. Note any pre-existing warnings/failures as baseline (do not fix unrelated pre-existing issues).
Record all captured output and the baseline exit codes in this feature's `findings` field.
acceptance_criteria: `node scripts/i18n-audit.mjs --ci` runs to completion and its exit code is recorded.
Baseline key counts and any pre-existing audit warnings/failures are recorded in findings so later features can distinguish new regressions from pre-existing state.
findings:
BASELINE ESTABLISHED (no source changes made in this feature).

=== Environment ===
- node --version => v22.23.2 (host); .nvmrc pins 24 but the audit script is plain Node ESM and ran fine on v22.
- pnpm --version => 11.4.0
- git: branch main, single commit 6776b1d 'Initial commit'; only untracked path is .agents/ (task state).

=== `node scripts/i18n-audit.mjs --ci` => EXIT CODE 0 (PASS, primary gate) ===
Key counts (source of truth = en.ts):
  en     2019 keys (source of truth)
  ja     1163 keys (58%)
  zh     1163 keys (58%)
  vi     1163 keys (58%)
  pt-BR  1169 keys (58%)
  th     1163 keys (58%)
  fr     1178 keys (58%)
  ca     1178 keys (58%)
  es     1178 keys (58%)
  ru     1274 keys (63%)
Audited LOCALES array = [ja, zh, vi, pt-BR, th, fr, ca, es, ru] (en excluded as source of truth; any locale not in this array is NOT audited).

PRE-EXISTING baseline state (NOT regressions; --ci tolerates all of these):
- Missing keys (en.ts key absent in locale): ja 860, zh 860, vi 860, pt-BR 850, th 860, fr 841, ca 841, es 841, ru 755. Largest missing groups everywhere: connect.* (267), extensions.* (~168-170), settings.* (70-116). --ci does NOT fail on missing non-en keys (English fallback chain covers gaps).
- Orphan keys (in locale but not en.ts): NONE for any locale.
- Duplicate keys: NONE for any locale (incl. en).
- Unused keys warning: ~330 potentially unused en.ts keys (config.* 50, settings.* 40, connect.* 37, skills.* 35, extensions.* 28, den.* 24, etc.). This is a non-failing WARNING only. NOTE: one such key is `status.openwork_ready` (brand string flagged as potentially unused) - relevant to later rebrand features.
- Dangling t() calls: NONE (all t() keys exist in en.ts).
- Dynamic t() calls: NONE.
- Aliased t() calls: NONE (all use t() directly).
- Placeholder integrity: PASS (all placeholders preserved).
- Plural completeness: PASS for all locales (en, ja, zh, vi, pt-BR, th, fr, ca, es, ru).

=== `node scripts/i18n-audit.mjs --duplicates --dangling --placeholders --plurals` => EXIT CODE 0 (PASS) ===
Same key counts as above. Duplicate keys: NONE for any locale. No failures reported.

=== Baseline conclusion ===
Both audit invocations exit 0 on a clean tree. The failing checks (duplicates, dangling t() refs, placeholder mismatches, incomplete plurals) are all currently GREEN, so any FAIL introduced by later features (zh removal, ko addition, rebrand) is a NEW regression attributable to that change. Missing-key counts and the ~330 unused-key warning are pre-existing and expected; they must not be treated as regressions. When 'ko' is added it must also be appended to the audit's hardcoded LOCALES array to be covered; when 'zh' is removed it should be dropped from that array so its 1163 baseline keys stop being reported.
